title: NodeChannel IID validation breaks multi-hop mesh routing
description:
IID validation at node_channel.py:202 compares link-layer sender's IID against IPv6 source IID. In multi-hop scenarios (which NodeChannel explicitly supports per docstring), the link-layer sender is the forwarding node, not the original source. This causes ALL multi-hop packets to be dropped.

The SCHC payload preserves the original IPv6 source, but rx.sender (from node.py:449) is the immediate link-layer neighbor. The integration test test_coap_get_via_relay fails due to unrelated API changes, leaving this code path untested.

**Options:**
1. Remove IID check and require OSCORE for all traffic
2. Accept packets where sender != source when OSCORE-protected
3. Document NodeChannel as single-hop only and create a separate channel for relayed traffic

**Cannot simply remove the check** - that would enable source spoofing from direct neighbors.

This requires architectural decision on how E2E authentication (OSCORE) should interact with link-layer authentication.
close_reason: Already fixed: Python node_channel.py has correct multi-hop model (no IID check, relies on OSCORE for E2E auth). Comment at lines 204-210 documents security model.
